metaDescription: Five rechargeable electric lint removers compared by blade design, speeds, battery life and size, for pilling on sweaters, blankets and furniture.
introParagraphs: Electric lint removers, often sold as fabric shavers or defuzzers, solve a problem that sticky rollers cannot: the small balls of fiber that form on sweaters, blankets and couch cushions as they wear. A roller lifts loose lint, but a shaver trims the pills off the surface. We compared five rechargeable models that suit a home with a few knit sweaters and a well used couch.

The differences are in battery, blades and size. The Electrolux full size model has a 2000 mAh battery and runs up to 180 minutes, while its compact sibling has a 1200 mAh battery in a body that measures 2.5 by 2.25 by 5.5 inches. The BEAUTURAL spins at 9000 RPM with a 6 leaf blade, and the Peiyuu and ASNUG both pair 6 leaf blades with three speeds and an LED display.

We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at battery, blade design, speed control and fabric safety. The sections below explain how to match a shaver to knitwear, upholstery or travel, instead of simply ranking by features.

products.name: Electrolux Rechargeable Fabric Shaver, 3 Speed
products.description:
The full size Electrolux is the most capable electric lint remover in this group. It offers three adjustable speed settings, so you can slow it down for delicate fabrics and speed it up for thicker garments and furniture. A 2000 mAh lithium ion battery supports up to 180 minutes of use on a single charge, which is long enough to do a whole closet.

An LED display shows battery life, speed level and charging status at a glance, and Type-C fast charging makes topping up easy. The tradeoff is size, because the full size body is bulkier than the compact model, and it still needs a light touch on loose knits. The listing frames it for clothes and furniture.

Cleaning means emptying the lint chamber after use, and it stores easily in a drawer. Compared with the compact Electrolux, you get a bigger battery and a larger body for the same three speeds. Against the BEAUTURAL, you gain a display and a longer stated runtime.
products.bestFor: Whole wardrobe and furniture refresh sessions
pros: Three speeds for delicate and heavy fabrics
2000 mAh battery runs up to 180 minutes
LED display shows battery, speed and charging
Type-C fast charging
cons: Needs a light touch on loose knits

products.name: BEAUTURAL Rechargeable Fabric Shaver, 6-Leaf
products.description:
The BEAUTURAL stands out for a steady motor. It spins at 9000 rotations per minute, and the seller says the speed stays stable regardless of battery power, so the cutting performance does not fade as the charge drops. Six leaf blades are described as doubling cleaning efficiency compared with a 3 blade cutter head.

The battery runs over two hours of continuous use and charges in about 1.5 hours, and a low battery alert tells you when to plug in. The tradeoff is that the listing does not mention adjustable speeds in the details we reviewed, so it is a one setting machine, and extra care is needed on delicate knits. It also lacks the Type-C charging and LED display of the Electrolux.

Cleaning is emptying the lint chamber, and the blade head is easy to access. Compared with the full size Electrolux, you give up speed options and a display. Against the ASNUG, you gain a steady motor but lose the digital readout.
products.bestFor: Consistent performance across a long session
pros: Stable 9000 RPM motor regardless of battery
Six leaf blades for faster cleanup
Runs over two hours per charge
Low battery alert
cons: No adjustable speeds in the listing

products.name: Electrolux Compact Travel Fabric Shaver
products.description:
The compact Electrolux is the one to pick if size matters. It measures only 2.5 by 2.25 by 5.5 inches, so it slips into bags, pocketbooks and drawers. Despite the small body, it keeps three adjustable speed settings and a 6 leaf blade for faster cleanup.

The 1200 mAh lithium ion battery charges over Type-C, which makes travel charging simple. The tradeoff is battery size, since 1200 mAh is smaller than the 2000 mAh in its sibling, so a long session will need a recharge. The smaller head also covers less area per pass, which matters on large blankets.

Cleaning is emptying the lint chamber, and storage is easy. Compared with the full size Electrolux, you give up battery and head size for portability. Against the Peiyuu, you get a compact body and a trusted brand, but not the LED display.
products.bestFor: Travel, suitcases and quick fixes before an event
pros: Measures just 2.5 x 2.25 x 5.5 inches
Three speeds in a compact body
Six leaf blade for faster cleanup
Type-C charging

products.name: Peiyuu Rechargeable Fabric Shaver, 6-Leaf
products.description:
The Peiyuu is aimed at the full range of home textiles. The listing says it is made for removing fuzz, pills and lint from sweaters, blankets, curtains, carpets, furniture and couches. Six leaf blades are described as razor sharp and doubling cleaning efficiency compared with a 3 blade head, with three speeds to match different fabrics.

A digital LED display lets you monitor the battery level and speed setting, which helps you avoid running out of charge mid job. The tradeoff is that the listing gives little detail about battery capacity or runtime in the information we reviewed, so you cannot compare it directly with the Electrolux. It is also an unfamiliar brand with less track record.

Cleaning is emptying the lint chamber, and the unit is easy to store. Compared with the ASNUG, the feature set is very similar, so the choice comes down to price and availability. Against the Electrolux, you get the same speeds and display but without the stated battery life.
products.bestFor: Curtains, couches and blankets as well as clothes
pros: Six leaf blades for faster cleanup
Three speeds suit different fabrics
LED display shows battery and speed
Designed for curtains, carpets and furniture
cons: Battery capacity and runtime are not stated

products.name: ASNUG Electric Fabric Shaver, 6-Leaf
products.description:
The ASNUG makes speed control as simple as pressing the power button. The listing says one touch adjustment cycles through three speed settings for different fabrics, and a 6 leaf blade design pairs with a high efficiency motor to remove lint and pills. An LED digital display shows what the unit is doing.

The seller markets it for both family and travel use, saying it can tidy a favorite sweater before heading out or keep a living room sofa looking neat. The tradeoff is that battery details are not given in the information we reviewed, and the single button for power and speed can be confusing at first. It is a competent, no frills option.

Cleaning is emptying the lint chamber, and storage is easy. Compared with the Peiyuu, the feature set is nearly identical, so the one touch speed control is the main differentiator. Against the BEAUTURAL, you get three speeds and a display but not the stated steady motor.
products.bestFor: Simple speed control for sweaters and sofas
pros: One touch speed change on the power button
Six leaf blade with a high efficiency motor
LED digital display
Suited to sweaters and sofas
cons: Single button for power and speed takes learning

buyingCriteria.criterion: Understand what a shaver can and cannot do
buyingCriteria.explanation: An electric lint remover trims fabric pills with spinning blades, which is different from a sticky roller that lifts loose lint and hair. The BEAUTURAL and Electrolux listings focus on fuzz and pilling, not pet hair. Use the shaver on sweaters, blankets and upholstery, and a roller for loose hair. Always test on a hidden spot first.

More blades usually means faster cleanup and a smoother result. The BEAUTURAL, Peiyuu, ASNUG and compact Electrolux use 6 leaf blades, described as doubling efficiency compared with a 3 blade head. A sharp, replaceable blade lasts longer. Replace blades when the results dull.

Slower speeds protect delicate knits, while faster speeds handle thicker fabrics. The Electrolux, Peiyuu and ASNUG each offer three speeds. The BEAUTURAL listing gives only a 9000 RPM motor. Use the lowest speed on loose weaves to avoid snagging.

The Electrolux has a 2000 mAh battery with up to 180 minutes, the compact Electrolux has 1200 mAh, and the BEAUTURAL runs over two hours with a 1.5 hour charge. Other listings do not state a figure. Type-C charging, found on both Electrolux models, is convenient. Plan the battery against the size of your project.

A compact body like the 2.5 by 2.25 by 5.5 inch Electrolux fits a bag, while a full size body covers more area per pass. A lightweight, easy to hold shaver is better for anyone with a weaker grip. A larger head helps with blankets. Choose the size that suits your main use.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Think about the display and cleanup
buyingCriteria.explanation: An LED display like those on the Electrolux, Peiyuu and ASNUG shows battery and speed. A lint chamber that empties easily saves time. Empty it after each session so it does not clog. Check that the blade head is easy to access.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade and motor
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade count and motor details, from the 6 leaf blades on four picks to the BEAUTURAL's stable 9000 RPM motor. We checked how clearly each listing explains its cutting system. Clarity and efficiency scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and charging
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the stated capacity and runtime, such as the Electrolux's 2000 mAh and 180 minutes. We noted which listings gave no figure. Type-C charging was a plus.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed control and fabric safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed the number of speeds and how they are controlled. The Electrolux and ASNUG offer three speeds. Fabric safety guidance counted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dimensions and weight, with the compact Electrolux at 2.5 by 2.25 by 5.5 inches setting the benchmark. Portable designs scored for travel. Weight and grip comfort were noted for anyone with weaker hands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Strongest versus most basic pick
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the full size Electrolux, with its three speeds, 2000 mAh battery and display, against the ASNUG, which gives little battery detail. The Electrolux earns Best Overall for specs and clarity, while the ASNUG is a simple alternative. Value and ease of use were weighed alongside the feature gap.

cards.label: Full size
cards.text: The full size Electrolux, Peiyuu, ASNUG and BEAUTURAL cover more area per pass and usually carry larger batteries. They are better for blankets and sofas. Choose these for home use.

cards.label: Compact
cards.text: The compact Electrolux fits a bag and handles clothes quickly, but has a smaller battery and head. Recommendation: pick a full size for home textiles, and the compact for travel.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Adjustable speeds, a sharp multi blade head and a light touch. Always test on a hidden spot and avoid pressing hard.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Electrolux 3-speed suits best, with a low speed for delicate knits. The compact Electrolux is the alternative for travel.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You own lots of knitwear or want a long battery. The Electrolux full size model gives three speeds, a display and up to 180 minutes of use.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need occasional pill removal. The ASNUG and BEAUTURAL cover basic needs at lower cost.

faq.q: How do I choose between an electric lint remover and a lint roller?
faq.a: A roller lifts loose lint and hair, while an electric remover trims the pills that form on worn fabric. If a sweater has fuzzy balls, use a shaver like the Electrolux. If the problem is loose hair, a roller is better.
They range from the lowest-cost ASNUG to the premium Electrolux. The price often tracks battery size and brand. Check the current price on Amazon before deciding, since it changes often.
It can if you press too hard or use a high speed on a loose weave. Start on the lowest speed, such as on the Electrolux, and keep the head flat and moving. Test a hidden spot first.

faq.q: Can I use it on pet hair?
faq.a: Shavers trim pills and fuzz, and the BEAUTURAL line is described as not for pet hair. A sticky roller is the better tool for loose hair. Many households use both.

faq.q: How do I care for the blades?
faq.a: Empty the lint chamber after each use and clean the blade head gently with the brush supplied, if one is included. Replace blades when results dull. Charge the battery before storage.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: The Electrolux full size model lists up to 180 minutes, and the BEAUTURAL over two hours. The compact Electrolux has a smaller 1200 mAh battery. Plan your project length around the stated runtime and charge in advance.
